title: How Frank Sinatra Lost His Nevada Gaming License
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Giancana at Cal-Neva and the 1963 Gaming Control Board action
quote: Sinatra surrendered his gaming licenses for the Cal-Neva and for the Sands on the Las Vegas Strip, where he also held an interest.
summary: Historian's account: Giancana, on Nevada's List of Excluded Persons, was found at the Cal-Neva in summer 1963 as Sinatra's guest; the Gaming Control Board filed a complaint and Sinatra gave up his licenses.
limits: Radio script quoting a 2001 oral-history interview with a former gaming control official; shows a guest visit, not Giancana ownership.

title: Frank Sinatra FBI Files (FBI Vault release, archive.org full text)
venue: FBI Vault release, hosted at Internet Archive
ask_addressed: mob-tie: FBI record of Giancana at the Cal-Neva and loss of Nevada licenses
quote: he surrendered his gambling licenses in Nevada when it was discovered that he had entertained Sam Giancana of the Chicago underworld at the Cal-Neva
summary: FBI summary in the Sinatra file records that he surrendered his Nevada gambling licenses after entertaining Giancana at the Cal-Neva. The same file also records the Cal-Neva being bought by the Sinatra group in 1961 and Paul D'Amato in charge of gambling there.
limits: OCR of a scanned file; a 1962 Chicago-office entry elsewhere in the file (sinatr5 volume) says earlier reporting held the Lodge was jointly owned by Giancana and Sinatra, which is informant reporting the FBI did not verify, so ownership by Giancana stays alleged. The scan is a hosted copy, not the vault.fbi.gov page.

title: Gaming Regulation in Nevada (UNOHP Catalog #236)
venue: University of Nevada Oral History Program
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Giancana as guest of the licensed owner; Black Book
quote: visited Lake Tahoe's Cal-Neva Lodge anyway as a guest of the resort's licensed owner: Frank Sinatra.
summary: University oral-history volume (foreword) describes the Black Book, Giancana's visit to the Cal-Neva as Sinatra's guest, and that Sinatra gave up his license. It calls Sinatra 'rumored' to be Giancana's front man, not proven.
limits: Interview-based volume, 2001-2004 interviews published 2016; a rumor of fronting is reported as rumor only.

title: Allegations of mob ties haunted the chairman
ask_addressed: mob-tie: sceptical, Sinatra's denial that the Cal-Neva was a mob front
quote: said the property was not a front for the mob's hidden interests
summary: Reports Sinatra's 1981 Gaming Control Board testimony denying he invited Giancana to the Cal-Neva in 1963 and denying the property was a mob front; the Gaming Commission later granted him an unrestricted licence. Also states he surrendered his licence in 1963 over alleged Giancana ties.
limits: Denial by the person concerned, who is now deceased; a denial is not a finding. Sceptical only on ownership, not on the 1963 events.

title: Frank Sinatra's Lake Tahoe casino shuts down
ask_addressed: dates: closing of the Cal-Neva casino in 2010
quote: On Wednesday, roulette wheels will stop spinning and blackjack games will cease at Sinatra's old resort
summary: Casino gaming at the Cal Neva stopped in April 2010 (item dated April 9, 2010; exact day not stated beyond 'Wednesday').
limits: Gives no explicit calendar date for the Wednesday; the resort was not yet closed.

title: Sinatra's old Lake Tahoe resort to get major makeover
ask_addressed: dates: closure of the resort in September 2013 and 2010 casino shutdown; lineage
quote: Its casino was forced to shut down in 2010 due to declining business.
summary: AP says Criswell-Radovan acquired the Cal Neva in April 2013 and the hotel-casino would close for more than a year from Monday (Sept 9, 2013). Says Sinatra owned it 1960 to 1963; mentions tunnels used to move 'mobsters and celebrities'.
limits: Tunnel claim is stated without attribution; 1960-1963 conflicts with Wikipedia's 1960-1968 (sale in 1968 after lease to Warner).

title: Cal Neva Lodge & Casino
ask_addressed: lineage: owners and names of the Cal Neva 1926 to 2023
quote: Sinatra publicly bought the resort in 1960 through his company, Park Lake Enterprises.
summary: Ownership chain: Sherman 1926; Remmer group 1935; Adler (renamed Cal Neva) c.1945-48; Grober group 1955; Park Lake Enterprises 1960; Warner lease; 1968 sale; BKJ 1975; Kerkorian 1976; Bluth 1985; Namvar 2005; Criswell-Radovan 2013; Ellison 2018; McWhinney 2023.
limits: Wikipedia, context only. Its lead says Giancana was a partner and that Sinatra's licence was 'suspended', which the primary and historian sources above describe as a surrender; lead and body differ on closing (2010 vs 2013).

title: Harolds Club
ask_addressed: dates and lineage: Smith family to Hughes (1970) and later owners; no mob tie
quote: In June 1970, the family sold the club to billionaire Howard Hughes
summary: Opened Feb 23, 1935; 1962 sale-leaseback to Webbel Corporation; sold to Hughes June 1970; Howard Hughes Corporation sold to The Fitzgerald Group in 1988; Gamma International 1995; closed March 31, 1995; Harrah's imploded it Dec 16, 1999. It describes the club's reputation as 'clean, friendly' and mentions no organised-crime tie.
limits: Absence of a mob mention in one encyclopedia entry is not proof; page last updated May 15, 2015.

title: Harolds Club in Reno to be demolished
ask_addressed: dates: demolition in December 1999 by Harrah's
quote: the seven-story building will be imploded by its new owners Harrah's Entertainment Inc.
summary: Demolition set for Wednesday Dec 15, 1999 by Harrah's Entertainment; describes the club as founded 1935 by the Smith family, with a reputation for innovation and scholarships.
limits: Does not address organised crime either way. Online Nevada gives Dec 16 for the implosion; the Sun item (dated Dec 14) says Wednesday, which was Dec 15.

title: Harold's Club
quote: The casino closed in 1995 and the building was demolished in 1999.
summary: Gives sale to Howard Hughes's Summa Corporation in 1970 for $11.5 million and to Gamma International in December 1994.
limits: Wikipedia, context only; says Dec 1994 sale and closing three months later.

title: Every Light Was On: Bill Harrah and His Clubs Remembered
venue: University of Nevada Oral History Program
ask_addressed: dates and lineage: Harrah's Reno from 1937 bingo parlor to Holiday Inns takeover
quote: Harrahs rise in the world of gaming began in 1946 when he went deeply into debt to become the sole owner and operator
summary: Introduction: bingo parlor in Reno in 1937, casino named Harrahs Reno Club in 1946, Tahoe club 1955, Golden Hotel tower 1969, NYSE listing 1973, acquisition by Holiday Inns in 1980.
limits: Oral-history introduction; the 1937 date is for a small bingo parlor, the casino as such dates from 1946.

title: Every Light Was On: Bill Harrah and His Clubs Remembered (Drews interview)
venue: University of Nevada Oral History Program
ask_addressed: mob-tie: sceptical, Harrah's persuaded financiers it was not mob-owned
quote: was not owned and operated by gangsters and hoodlums
summary: Introductory summary says Harrah's management persuaded New York financiers the company was legitimate and not owned and operated by gangsters and hoodlums; an interviewee notes everyone suspected Mafia ties when seeking a bond rating.
limits: Company-insider oral history, not an independent finding; stronger evidence would be a Gaming Control Board or SEC record.

title: Harrah's Reno
ask_addressed: dates: closure in 2020; lineage through Holiday Inn, Vici, CAI
quote: In June 2020, Caesars announced that it would not reopen Harrah's Reno.
summary: Closed March 17, 2020 under a COVID order and did not reopen; Holiday Inn owned it from 1981; Vici took ownership Oct 2017 with lease to Caesars; sale to CAI finalized Sept 2020.
limits: Wikipedia, context only; 'More citations needed' tag. Closure date for the casino should be confirmed from a news or Nevada gaming source.

title: Mapes Hotel and Casino, Reno
ask_addressed: dates and lineage: Mapes family, 1982 foreclosure, 1988 sale, 1996 city, 2000 demolition
quote: The Mapes officially opened on December 17, 1947.
summary: Built by the Mapes family and financed by Bank of America, First National Bank of Nevada and the RFC; foreclosed December 1982; bought June 1988 by Karadanis and Maloff; sold to Reno Redevelopment Agency 1996; imploded January 30, 2000. No organised-crime tie is mentioned.
limits: Absence from one encyclopedia entry is not proof.

title: Mapes Hotel
quote: The Mapes casino closed on December 17, 1982
summary: Describes Mapes-family ownership throughout the casino years, failure after the 1981 recession and the Money Tree, then several owners and city purchase in 1996.

title: Investigation of Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce: index to hearings (Kefauver Committee)
authors: U.S. Senate Special Committee to Investigate Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Kefauver 1950-51 hearing index entries for Reno properties
summary: The hearings index has an entry for the Mapes Hotel, Reno (pages in Pt. 2 and Pt. 12). My text search of the OCR index found no entries for Harold's Club, Harrah's or the Cal-Neva.
limits: Index entry only. I did not open the cited hearing pages, so the context of the Mapes mention is unknown and it is not evidence of a tie. OCR of the index is imperfect, so absence of the other names is suggestive only.
